## The waffle

<!--
Beat 1 - Hook. The viral 2,500-dot chart (Damian Player, Feb 2026):
84% grey never-used, green free tier, yellow sliver of paid, one red
dot for AI coding-tool users. Caption culture: "you're early".
Establish the chart quickly; the full stats-pedant critique lives in
the companion piece / appendix, not here. One or two sentences of
acknowledgement that the numbers were off (denominator error, paid and
coding tiers undercounted 3-4x) with the corrected version shown below.
-->

[Jon: opening beat - introduce the viral chart and what everyone took from it]

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)

n_side <- 50L
n_dots <- n_side^2

df <- read_csv("assets/ai_adoption_timeseries.csv") |>
  select(snapshot_date, category, value_millions) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = value_millions) |>
  mutate(
    coding  = coding_tool_users,
    paid    = pmax(paid_subscribers - coding_tool_users, 0),
    free    = pmax(genai_users_ever - paid_subscribers, 0),
    offline = offline_no_internet,
    never_online = world_population - genai_users_ever - offline_no_internet
  ) |>
  select(snapshot_date, world_population,
         offline, never_online, free, paid, coding) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(snapshot_date, world_population),
               names_to = "tier", values_to = "millions") |>
  mutate(tier = factor(
    tier,
    levels = c("offline", "never_online", "free", "paid", "coding"),
    labels = c("Offline (no internet)", "Online, never used gen AI",
               "Free-tier user", "Paid subscriber", "Coding-tool user")
  ))

allocate_dots <- function(millions, total_millions, n = n_dots) {
  raw   <- millions / total_millions * n
  base  <- floor(raw)
  base  <- if_else(millions > 0 & base == 0, 1, base)
  short <- n - sum(base)
  rem   <- raw - floor(raw)
  order_idx <- order(rem, decreasing = TRUE)
  add <- integer(length(millions))
  if (short > 0) add[order_idx[seq_len(short)]] <- 1L
  if (short < 0) {
    big <- order(base, decreasing = TRUE)
    add[big[seq_len(-short)]] <- -1L
  }
  base + add
}

grid <- df |>
  group_by(snapshot_date) |>
  mutate(dots = allocate_dots(millions, first(world_population))) |>
  reframe(tier = rep(tier, dots)) |>
  group_by(snapshot_date) |>
  mutate(idx = row_number() - 1L,
         col = idx %% n_side,
         row = idx %/% n_side) |>
  ungroup()

pal <- c(
  "Offline (no internet)"     = "#A89F93",
  "Online, never used gen AI" = "#D9D5CD",
  "Free-tier user"            = "#6FA877",
  "Paid subscriber"           = "#D9A441",
  "Coding-tool user"          = "#B5493F"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-waffle-latest
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The corrected version of the viral chart, March 2026: right
#|   denominator, paid and coding tiers scaled to reported subscriber
#|   figures, and the offline population split out of the grey monolith.
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
latest <- max(grid$snapshot_date)
pop_latest <- df |>
  filter(snapshot_date == latest) |>
  pull(world_population) |>
  first()

grid |>
  filter(snapshot_date == latest) |>
  ggplot(aes(col, -row, fill = tier)) +
  geom_tile(width = 0.82, height = 0.82) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, name = NULL) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_void(base_family = "mono") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(family = "serif", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5,
                                     colour = "grey40")) +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Each dot is ~%.1f million people",
                    pop_latest / n_dots),
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "2,500 dots = %.2f billion humans. Colour = deepest gen-AI engagement, %s.",
      pop_latest / 1000, format(latest, "%b %Y"))
  )
```

## What the tiers actually measure

<!--
Beat 2 - Pivot from "how many" to "what kind". The chart's tiers read
as a spending ladder (free < $20/month < coding tools), but the more
interesting reading is that they are tiers of *embodiment*: how much
of the world the model has been given hands to act on.
This is where P1 lands: the practical gulf between a bare LLM - a
brain you talk to through a letterbox - and an agentically scaffolded
one, with tools, a file system, an execution loop, memory, the ability
to check its own work. Same brain, radically different practical
utility. Possible concrete contrasts: asking a chatbot to describe a
fix vs an agent applying, testing and committing it; copy-paste
round-tripping vs direct action.
-->

[Jon: develop P1 - the free/paid/coding split is really a
disembodied/embodied split, and the practical difference is enormous]

## Krang

<!--
Beat 3 - P2, the central image. Krang from Teenage Mutant Ninja
Turtles: a warlord reduced to a disembodied brain - clever, malevolent,
shouty, and almost completely impotent - who becomes formidable only
when installed in the belly of an android exoskeleton built for him.
The LLM is Krang-the-brain; the agentic scaffold is the exoskeleton.
Why this image is *efficient*: it carries in one picture (a) the brain
is not diminished by needing the body, (b) the body without the brain
is inert, (c) the combination is a different order of thing than
either part, and (d) the brain famously sits in the robot's *stomach*,
visibly a component, not a soul - which is more honest than most
AI metaphors manage.
Optional: image of Krang here - need a copyright-safe option; a
hand-drawn sketch would be very on-brand for this blog.
-->

[Jon: develop P2 - Krang as the most efficient single pop-cultural
image of the scaffold/LLM distinction]

## Rereading the red dot

<!--
Beat 4 - Synthesis. Bring the two together: the red dot (coding-tool
users, ~6-10M overlap-adjusted) is not just the top of a pricing
ladder; it is, to a first approximation, the set of people who have
used a brain *with a body*. Nearly everyone's mental model of "AI" -
including most of the green band's - is formed on the disembodied
version. Implications to consider: public debate about AI capability
is mostly debate about Krang-in-a-jar; the diffusion story that
matters may be exoskeleton diffusion, not brain access, and the chart
has no way to show that a body can be handed to anyone already
holding a brain.
-->

[Jon: synthesis - what the red dot means once you've got the Krang
frame, and why the interesting diffusion curve is the one the chart
can't show]
